title: an UNDECLARED `_name` sitting in $fpath is executable on zshrs — zsh reports command not found, zshrs autoloads the file, runs it and leaves the function defined

observed.one_sided: zsh also writes `zsh:2: command not found: _zzimpl` to stderr; stderr is not compared here (the two shells prefix diagnostics differently, `probe.zsh:2:` against `zsh:2:`) so the evidence is taken from stdout: the rc=127/rc=0 split and the `defined=` count say the same thing without dragging an unrelated divergence into the cell.
observed.notes: It is not an exec: the file is mode 0644 and has no #! line, and afterwards `${+functions[_zzimpl]}` is 1 on zshrs — the shell autoloaded it as a function on command-not-found because its name is in $fpath. `whence -w _zzimpl` says `none` on BOTH shells before the call, so the divergence is at execution, not in the lookup table. The two controls place the variable: the same file under a name with no leading underscore is not run (both shells: command not found), and with `fpath=( )` the underscore name is not run either. Measured separately in round 6: `__zz` (two underscores) is also run, so the trigger is a leading `_`, not the exact name. What it costs in practice: every completer in the user's fpath becomes a command, so a typo'd or shadowing `_name` on the command line executes completion code instead of failing.

controls.note: same file, same directory, name WITHOUT the leading underscore. Agrees (PASS): both shells report rc=127 defined=0, so it is the `_` prefix that is load-bearing
the same underscore name with an EMPTY fpath. Agrees (PASS), so the file is reached through $fpath and nothing else

origin: reported in round 5 as `fpath=(DIR)` with `DIR/_zzimpl` and no autoload being executable on zshrs
